name: Squire Sawyer Whateley
summary: Squire Sawyer Whateley, chairman of the local draft board in 1917, struggled to find enough physically sound young Dunwich men to fill even a development-camp quota, an early hint of the region's degeneracy.
description: When war came in 1917, Squire Sawyer Whateley, as chairman of the local draft board, had hard work finding a quota of young Dunwich men fit even to be sent to a development camp — a telling sign of the region's inbred decline.
